title: Nagelsmann quits as Germany coach after early World Cup 2026 exit
facts: Julian Nagelsmann stepped down as the coach of the Germany national football team on July 3, 2026.
Julian Nagelsmann's resignation followed Germany's elimination from the 2026 World Cup by Paraguay.
Paraguay defeated Germany 4-3 on penalty kicks during the knockout stages of the 2026 World Cup.
The German Football Association confirmed Julian Nagelsmann's departure following talks with senior officials.
Julian Nagelsmann's contract with the German national football team was originally set to last until the 2028 European Championship.
Bernd Neuendorf is the President of the German Football Association.
The German tabloid Bild reported that Julian Nagelsmann was offered a seven-million-euro severance package to leave his coaching position.
Julian Nagelsmann is only the second national coach in German history to be forced to step down.
Hansi Flick was the first national coach in German history to be forced to step down in 2023.
The German national football team suffered group-stage exits at the 2018 World Cup in Russia and the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.
The German national football team has not won a knockout match at a World Cup tournament since the 2014 final.
The German Football Association identified Jurgen Klopp as their preferred candidate to replace Julian Nagelsmann.
Jurgen Klopp has publicly stated that he is fundamentally willing to take over as the Germany national football team coach.
Jurgen Klopp currently serves as Red Bull's global head of football.
Jurgen Klopp's contract with Red Bull reportedly includes a release clause allowing him to take the Germany national team coaching job.
